overall_summary: Deduplication and recency weighting show that space and planetary 'what-if' scenarios are vastly outperforming other categories in views-per-day and engagement. Videos published within the last 7 to 10 days, particularly speculative extreme space scenarios (e.g., liquid diamond planets, dark planets, and planetary comparisons), achieve significantly higher velocity and like-per-view ratios than older psychology, biology, or standard fact shorts.

winning_patterns.pattern: Speculative Planetary 'What If' / Extreme Space Scenarios
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (YlDuGu1vzAg) generated high views (800-1000+) and strong like ratios within short windows compared to older static facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space disaster/immersion scenarios focusing on bizarre exoplanets with extreme physical properties.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) drove over 900-1000 views with strong engagement due to counterintuitive cosmic time or light facts.
winning_patterns.action: Use stark, paradoxical comparisons involving planetary physics, time distortion, or light absorption in titles.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A, 5 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (Jc04LVKNd2s, 17 views) heavily underperformed compared to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological tricks and basic animal facts unless framed with high-stakes cinematic mystery or 'what-if' framing.

weak_patterns.evidence: Older historical mysteries like 'The 2,000-Year-Old Mystery Science Can't Solve' plateaued early with minimal likes and zero comments.
weak_patterns.action: Shift historical or archaeological concepts into high-tension micro-drama or unknown anomaly storytelling rather than dry trivia.

next_video.hook_style: Hypothetical sensory survival / Extreme physics what-if
next_video.concept: What If You Stepped Onto a Planet Made Entirely of Boiling Ice?
next_video.opening_direction: Start immediately with the violent sensory immersion of standing on a world where ice burns at thousands of degrees.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the extreme pressure keeps the boiling water completely solid beneath your boots until a microscopic crack forms.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high-performing 'What If' planetary immersion format while introducing a completely fresh exoplanet physical phenomenon not yet covered.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not repeat diamond planets, dark planets, rain of metals/rubies, or basic silent space facts.
Must use a newly introduced exoplanet paradox or theoretical thermodynamic anomaly.
Keep pacing under 20 seconds with high visual vocabulary.

experiment: Test a 21-second speculative physics 'what-if' scenario featuring a lesser-known cosmic anomaly (hot ice / superionic water) against standard planetary rain facts to test if immersion-based narration drives higher retention than descriptive narration.
